text: Autoinfection is a recognized means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must pass through a snail intermediate host
No - the egg must embryonate in moist soil for 2-3 weeks before it is infective
Yes - the larva inside the egg becomes infective within about 6 hours on the perianal skin, and scratching carries eggs to the mouth
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae inside the intestine
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larva penetrates the colonic wall
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) eggs are laid on the perianal skin by nocturnal migrating gravid females. The coiled tadpole-like larva develops into the infective third-stage larva within only 4 to 6 hours at body temperature, allowing retrofection or external autoinfection via contaminated fingers after scratching.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis autoinfection: Rapid perianal embryonation in 6 hours enables direct fecal-oral autoinfection.

text: This worm came out through the nose of a child after general anesthesia. Which figure represents the stage found on his stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Migration of adult Ascaris lumbricoides through the mouth or nose is a classic feature of anesthesia or pyrexia. Figure A represents the fertilized Ascaris egg: golden-brown, broadly oval, surrounded by a thick, bile-stained, coarsely mammillated albuminous coat containing an unsegmented ovum.
keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides: Adult erratic migration; stool shows characteristic mammillated fertilized eggs.

text: Rectal prolapse is a complication of heavy infection with this worm. Interpret.
options: Chronic blood loss causes atrophy of the anal sphincter
Gravid females migrate out at night, causing straining during sleep
A bolus of entangled adult worms obstructs the rectum and pushes it outwards
Flask-shaped ulcers weaken the rectal wall
The worm is deeply embedded in the mucosa by its thin anterior part, causing loss of muscle tone in heavy infection
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection (Trichuris dysentery syndrome), thousands of worms thread their attenuated anterior two-thirds into the cecal and rectal mucosa, eliciting chronic inflammation, loss of muscle tone, and tenesmus leading to rectal prolapse.
keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura: Attenuated anterior end threads into colonic mucosa, precipitating rectal prolapse in children.

text: A patient has hepatomegaly and jaundice. Three months ago he had fever, right upper quadrant pain and eosinophilia after eating green salads. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ingestion of green salads contaminated with encysted metacercariae leads to acute fascioliasis (biliary colic, high fever, eosinophilia, tender hepatomegaly). The diagnostic stage on stool examination is the Fasciola egg: large (140 x 80 µm), ellipsoidal, yellowish-brown, operculated, containing an unsegmented ovum surrounded by yolk cells.
keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica: Transmitted via encysted metacercariae on watercress; large operculated unsegmented egg.

text: Identify the station and what this stage does after leaving the snail:
options: Leptocercus cercaria of Heterophyes - encysts in fish muscle
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - penetrates human skin
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - encysts on aquatic plants
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - penetrates human skin
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - encysts on aquatic plants as a metacercaria
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola cercaria (leptocercus cercaria) has a simple, unbranched tail and dark cystogenous glands. Upon emergence from the Lymnaea snail, it encysts on emergent aquatic vegetation (watercress) to form the infective encysted metacercaria.
keyConcept: Fasciola cercaria: Leptocercus (simple tail), encysts on aquatic plants as metacercaria.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed part:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adult Echinococcus granulosus measures 3–6 mm and consists of only 3 proglottids: immature, mature, and a large terminal gravid segment (which occupies more than half of the total worm length and contains a branched sac-like uterus filled with eggs).
keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus adult: 3 segments (immature, mature, gravid); gravid segment > half total worm length.

text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must embryonate in soil for weeks
Yes - the egg is infective when passed and can hatch in the intestine, where the oncosphere develops into a cysticercoid in the villi
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae in the intestine
Yes - the egg needs about 6 hours on the perianal skin before it becomes infective
No - an insect intermediate host is always needed
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm) is the only human cestode capable of internal autoinfection: eggs released in the small intestine can hatch prematurely, releasing hexacanth oncospheres that invade the villi to develop into cysticercoids without exiting the host.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Only cestode with direct internal autoinfection (cysticercoids develop within intestinal villi).

text: In this cyst aspirate, the arrowed structures are the hooks of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hydatid sand examined microscopically consists of free hooklets, calcareous corpuscles, and invaginated protoscolices displaying a double row of hooklets and 4 suckers.
keyConcept: Hydatid sand: Protoscolices with characteristic double-crowned hooklets and suckers.

text: Food handlers are a serious source of this infection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the infection is transmitted only through water
No - the cyst must mature in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - asymptomatic carriers pass mature quadrinucleate cysts that are infective on passage and contaminate food
Yes - trophozoites survive on food and invade the colon
No - only trophozoites are passed, and they die quickly outside the body
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Food handlers shedding mature 4-nucleated Entamoeba histolytica or Giardia cysts are a major source of infection because the cysts are immediately infective upon passage, resistant to environmental chlorination, and easily transmitted via contaminated hands.
keyConcept: Amebiasis & Giardiasis: Asymptomatic cyst passers serve as key epidemiologic reservoirs.

text: Identify the adult worm and how it causes internal autoinfection:
options: Echinococcus granulosus - a ruptured hydatid cyst releases protoscolices that grow into adults
Diphyllobothrium latum - plerocercoids develop in the intestinal wall
Taenia saginata - reverse peristalsis carries gravid segments to the stomach
Hymenolepis nana - eggs hatch in the intestine and oncospheres develop into cysticercoids in the villi
Hymenolepis nana - it does not cause autoinfection; a flea or beetle intermediate host is obligatory
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana adult worm causes internal autoinfection when retained eggs hatch in the lumen and develop into tissue cysticercoids in the villi.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana internal autoinfection mechanism.

text: Structure 3 in this specimen is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 3 is the gynecophoric canal of the male Schistosoma: a ventral longitudinal groove formed by inrolled lateral margins extending from the ventral sucker to the posterior extremity, inside which the slender female is embraced.
keyConcept: Male Schistosoma gynecophoric canal: Ventral groove embracing female worm.

text: Identify the station:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex is cuboidal (1–2 mm in diameter), possesses 4 prominent hemispherical suckers, but completely lacks a rostellum and lacks hooks (unarmed scolex).
keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 suckers, NO rostellum, NO hooks (unarmed).

text: Structure 2 in this specimen is composed of:
options: Numerous follicular testes scattered in the body
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Male Schistosoma mansoni possesses 6 to 9 testes clustered in a compact zigzag mass situated dorsally behind the ventral sucker.
keyConcept: Male Schistosoma mansoni: 6–9 testes clustered in a mass.

text: Identify the egg and its arrowed content:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Male Schistosoma haematobium has 4-5 testes, while Heterophyes has 2 oval testes; male Schistosoma with testes arranged in a line.
keyConcept: Schistosoma testicular anatomy.

text: The middle arrow points to a structure that distinguishes this fluke from Metagonimus yokogawai. It is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Minute pyriform fluke (1.5 mm) with 3 suckers (oral sucker, ventral sucker, and a prominent genital sucker / gonotyl armed with 70–80 chitinous spinelets).
keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes: Minute fluke characterized by a third sucker (genital sucker / gonotyl).

text: Finding this egg in a single stool sample does not always mean active infection. Interpret.
options: The egg is a degenerated form that has lost its operculum
The egg is shed only in the acute (invasive) stage of the disease
The egg may pass transiently after eating infected raw liver , so stool is re-examined after a liver-free diet
The egg is shed only in bile, so duodenal aspirate is needed
The egg is identical to the Heterophyes egg, so serology is required
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large leaf-like fluke (up to 7 cm long) with parallel lateral margins, weakly developed cephalic cone, deeply branched intestinal caeca, and highly branched testes.
keyConcept: Fasciola gigantica: Large fluke with parallel margins, indistinct shoulders, and branched caeca.

text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - infection occurs only by skin penetration by filariform larvae
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larvae re-invade the mucosa
No - man is only an accidental host of this worm
No - the egg is passed with an unsegmented ovum and must embryonate in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - the mucoid plugs dissolve on the perianal skin and release infective larvae
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Modified Ziehl-Neelsen (Kinyoun) acid-fast stain showing bright pinkish-red, spherical, acid-fast oocysts measuring 4–5 µm against a blue-green background.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum: Acid-fast spherical oocysts (4–5 µm) on modified ZN stain.

text: A 31-year-old HIV-infected woman presents with severe watery diarrhea and dizziness. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: In HIV/AIDS patients with CD4 < 100, Cryptosporidium parvum causes cholera-like, profuse, secretory watery diarrhea leading to fatal dehydration. The acid-fast stain reveals characteristic spherical pink-red oocysts.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidiosis in AIDS: Intractable secretory watery diarrhea; diagnosed by acid-fast oocysts.

text: Which of these stages can cause internal autoinfection, so that the whole life cycle is completed inside one human host?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Stage capable of internal autoinfection causing persistent hyperinfection.
keyConcept: Internal autoinfection in parasitology.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large leaf-shaped fluke (3 cm) with distinct conical cephalic projection and prominent triangular shoulders.
keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica: Distinct cephalic cone and prominent shoulders.

text: Identify the station and the main reservoir of infection:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Active motility by rapid progressive unidirectional pseudopodia, single vesicular nucleus with central pinpoint karyosome, and ingested red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis, pathognomonic of invasive amebiasis).
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite: Erythrophagocytosis and central karyosome.

text: This parasite causes flask-shaped intestinal ulcers and extra-intestinal manifestations. Interpret.
options: Trophozoites lyse the mucosa with proteolytic enzymes, spread laterally in the submucosa, and reach the liver through the portal vein
Eggs lodge in the bowel wall and cause granulomas that ulcerate
Adult worms embed their anterior ends deep in the mucosa
Trophozoites burrow with their cilia and invade the lymphatics
Cysts excyst in the submucosa and grow into large colonies
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pear-shaped (tennis racket-shaped), bilateral symmetry, 2 large suction discs (adhesive discs), 2 nuclei ('face-like' appearance), and 4 pairs of flagella with falling-leaf motility.
keyConcept: Giardia lamblia trophozoite: Bilateral symmetry, 2 nuclei, 2 sucking discs, falling-leaf motility.

text: The snail that harbors the larval stages of this parasite is:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval shape, smooth thick cyst wall, 4 nuclei (often grouped at one pole), curved parabasal bodies, and longitudinal axonemes.
keyConcept: Giardia lamblia cyst: Oval, 4 nuclei, axostyle and curved parabasal bodies.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Entamoeba histolytica cyst - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with eccentric karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical cyst (10–15 µm) containing 1 to 4 nuclei with central pinpoint karyosomes, and cigar-shaped chromatoid bars with rounded ends.
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica mature cyst: Spherical, 4 nuclei, cigar-shaped chromatoid bodies.

text: Which feature distinguishes this fluke from Fasciola spp.?
options: Separate sexes with a gynecophoric canal
Branched intestinal caeca with a cephalic cone
Simple, unbranched intestinal caeca and no cephalic cone
A genital sucker beside the ventral sucker
A ventral sucker displaced to one side
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex equipped with 4 suckers and a rounded rostellum armed with a double crown of 22 to 32 alternating large and small hooks (armed scolex).
keyConcept: Taenia solium scolex: 4 suckers + rostellum with double crown of hooklets (armed).

text: Identify the egg and the source of infection:
options: Heterophyes heterophyes egg - raw or undercooked fish
Fasciola egg - raw or undercooked fish
Heterophyes heterophyes egg - aquatic plants such as watercress
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elongated rectangular segment (longer than broad) with a central median longitudinal uterine stem giving off 15 to 30 fine, dichotomously branched lateral uterine branches on each side.
keyConcept: Taenia saginata gravid segment: 15–30 lateral uterine branches (dichotomous branching).

text: A 4-year-old child has diarrhea with pale, loose, offensive, fatty stools and no mucus or blood. Which figure represents the stage found in a fresh diarrheic stool?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Giardiasis causes malabsorption syndrome with pale, greasy, foul-smelling diarrhea (steatorrhea) due to mechanical carpeting of the duodenal brush border. Figure represents the characteristic Giardia trophozoite/cyst.
keyConcept: Giardiasis: Duodenal brush border carpeting causing malabsorptive steatorrhea.

text: This parasite can be transmitted to humans by autoinfection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - this parasite infects only by larval skin penetration
Yes - the egg is infective on passage and is carried from the anus to the mouth
No - the egg can only infect after passing through Cyclops
Yes - the egg hatches in the small intestine and the larva migrates through the lungs again
No - the egg is passed with a one-cell ovum and needs about 2-3 weeks in soil to become embryonated
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid segment containing 7 to 12 coarse, dendritic, laterally branched uterine branches on each side.
keyConcept: Taenia solium gravid segment: 7–12 coarse lateral uterine branches.

text: Identify the station and its identifying criterion:
options: Entamoeba coli cyst - up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - 1-4 nuclei with central karyosomes
Giardia lamblia cyst - 4 nuclei and axostyles
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - up to 8 nuclei with central karyosomes
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Broader than long proglottid featuring a central rosette-shaped (coiled loop) uterus opening independently through a uterine pore.
keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum: Proglottid broader than long with central rosette-shaped uterus.

text: The arrowed structure in this larva is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slender cylindrical nematode with a curved anterior end and a prominent posterior umbrella-like copulatory bursa supported by 14 rays.
keyConcept: Male Ancylostoma duodenale: Copulatory bursa supported by rays.

text: Perianal swabbing is the method of choice for diagnosing infection with this egg. Interpret.
options: The eggs are very light and are lost from the surface of the stool sample
The gravid female migrates out of the anus at night and lays her eggs on the perianal skin,
Larvae from these eggs penetrate the perianal skin and stay there
The eggs hatch inside the colon, so only larvae reach the stool
The eggs are digested by colonic bacteria before they are passed
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tapered posterior end lacking a copulatory bursa, with vulva located near the junction of middle and posterior thirds.
keyConcept: Female Ancylostoma duodenale: Conical tapered tail.

text: Identify the specimen and the feature indicated by the lower arrow:
options: Strongyloides stercoralis female - tapering posterior end
Trichocephalus trichiurus female - blunt posterior end
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small white spindle-shaped worm (8–13 mm) with cephalic cuticular alae and a long, sharply pointed, pin-like tail.
keyConcept: Female Enterobius vermicularis: Pointed pin-like tail and cephalic alae.

text: Identify the station:
options: Female of Strongyloides stercoralis with eggs in uterus
Female of Enterobius vermicularis with eggs in uterus
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large roundworm (15–30 cm) with a ventrally curved posterior extremity equipped with two copulatory spicules.
keyConcept: Male Ascaris lumbricoides: Ventrally curved tail with 2 copulatory spicules.

text: Identify the station. Why can man harbor this stage?
options: Cysticercus cellulosae - man can act as an intermediate host
Cysticercus cellulosae - man is infected only by eating undercooked pork
Cysticercus bovis - reverse peristalsis brings gravid segments to the stomach
Hydatid cyst - man swallows eggs from dog feces
Cysticercus bovis - man is the normal intermediate host
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large roundworm (20–40 cm) with a straight, conical posterior extremity and genital girdle.
keyConcept: Female Ascaris lumbricoides: Straight tail, larger body.

text: This parasitic stage represents the infective stage of a case of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic whip-like morphology: attenuated, hair-like anterior three-fifths containing a stichosome cellular esophagus, and a thickened posterior two-fifths.
keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura: Whip-like shape with thin anterior and stout posterior body.

text: A 4-year-old child has pruritus ani, insomnia and nocturnal enuresis. Which figure represents the stage recovered by perianal swab?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Nocturnal pruritus ani and enuresis in children are diagnostic of Enterobius vermicularis. Figure represents the plano-convex D-shaped egg containing a folded larva.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis: Nocturnal perianal pruritus; D-shaped asymmetric egg.

text: An abdominal CT of a shepherd with right upper abdominal pain and no fever shows multiple cystic lesions of different sizes in both liver lobes. Which figure represents the stage found when the cyst fluid is examined?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Shepherd with hepatic hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus). Diagnostic stage is the hydatid sand containing protoscolices with double hooklet crowns.
keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus: Hepatic hydatid cyst in sheep-raising regions.

text: An Egyptian farmer presented with hematemesis, hepatosplenomegaly and ascites. Sonography showed severe periportal fibrosis. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination during the acute stage?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Farmer with portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and esophageal variceal bleeding due to Schistosoma mansoni. Diagnostic stage is the large oval egg with a sharp, prominent lateral spine.
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni: Lateral-spined egg causing periportal fibrosis and hematemesis.

text: Chronic blood loss in this infection is multifactorial. Interpret.
options: The worm competes with the host for vitamin B12 and folate in the jejunum
The worm sucks blood, and leaving bleeding points
Larvae damage the lung capillaries, causing repeated hemoptysis
Larvae migrate through the liver, causing bleeding esophageal varices
The worm secretes a hemolysin that lyses red cells inside the portal vessels
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, non-operculated, yellowish-brown egg (140 x 60 µm) with a prominent, sharp lateral spine near the posterior pole, containing a fully developed ciliated miracidium.
keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg: Large lateral spine and ciliated miracidium.

text: The structure indicated by the upper arrow is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spindle-shaped egg (150 x 50 µm) with a straight, sharp terminal spine at the posterior pole.
keyConcept: Schistosoma haematobium egg: Sharp terminal spine.

text: This snail is the intermediate host of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ellipsoidal operculated egg (140 x 80 µm) filled with uniform granular yolk cells surrounding an unsegmented ovum.
keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica egg: Operculated, unsegmented, large size.

text: This patient was admitted with diarrhea and abdominal pain. His skin had a diffuse, rapidly moving, erythematous reticular rash from the anal margin to the upper legs. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intestinal parasite causing diarrhea.
keyConcept: Diagnostic stage in stool examination.

text: Identify the station:
options: Balantidium coli cyst invading the mucosa
Cryptosporidium parvum stages on the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoite at the brush border
Balantidium coli cyst at the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoites invading the mucosa
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Minute, operculated, yellowish-brown egg (30 x 15 µm) with an indistinct opercular rim and a small knob-like thickening at the abopercular pole, containing a fully formed miracidium.
keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes egg: Minute (30 µm), operculated with abopercular knob, mature miracidium.

text: This snail is the first intermediate host of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical egg (35 µm) surrounded by a thick, brown, radially striated embryophore containing a 6-hooked hexacanth embryo (oncosphere).
keyConcept: Taenia egg: Thick radially striated embryophore with 6-hooked oncosphere.

text: Identify the station and the feature that identifies it:
options: Trichocephalus trichiurus in the appendix - bacillary band
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - double-bulbed esophagus seen in section
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - lateral cuticular alae
Ascaris lumbricoides in the appendix - thick cuticle
Strongyloides stercoralis in the mucosa - eggs in the uterus
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical or subspherical translucent egg (45 µm) with two distinct membranes: outer thin membrane and inner embryophore displaying two polar knobs from which 4 to 8 polar filaments emerge into the space.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana egg: Polar filaments emerging from polar knobs of embryophore.

text: Growth retardation may be a manifestation of this parasitic infection. Interpret.
options: A bolus of adult worms causes intestinal obstruction
The adult worm absorbs most of the dietary vitamin B12
Autoinfective larvae destroy the intestinal villi
Egg granulomas cause periportal hepatic fibrosis
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large yellowish-brown egg (70 µm) with inner and outer membranes but completely LACKING polar filaments.
keyConcept: Hymenolepis diminuta egg: Larger, no polar filaments.

text: A patient has fever, tenesmus and dysentery. Sigmoidoscopy shows ulcers with a narrow opening, raised edge and wide base. Which figure represents the stage found in the ulcer biopsy?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Amebic dysentery with flask-shaped colonic ulcers. Diagnostic stage is Entamoeba histolytica with erythrophagocytosis.
keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica: Flask-shaped ulcers and bloody dysentery.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Taenia spp. mature segment - bilobed ovary
Taenia saginata gravid segment - central uterine stem
Taenia solium gravid segment - lateral uterine branches
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - rosette-shaped uterus
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - bilobed ovary
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval operculated egg (70 x 45 µm) with an inconspicuous opercular cap and a small abopercular knob, containing an unsegmented ovum.
keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum egg: Operculated with abopercular knob, unsegmented.

text: Identify the station:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval egg (60 x 40 µm) with blunt rounded poles, an extremely thin, transparent, clear shell, and an internal segmented ovum (morula stage with 4 to 8 blastomeres) separated from the shell by a clear space.
keyConcept: Hookworm egg: Thin transparent shell with 4–8 blastomeres and clear space.

text: Structure 2 in this egg is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Round/oval egg with a thick transparent inner shell covered by a golden-brown, coarsely tuberculated (mammillated) albuminous coat, containing a single unsegmented ovum.
keyConcept: Fertilized Ascaris egg: Coarsely mammillated albuminous coat and unsegmented ovum.

text: Layer 1 in this section is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elongated, narrow, irregular egg (90 x 45 µm) with a thin shell and irregular mammillations filled with disorganized, highly refractile, atrophic yolk globules.
keyConcept: Unfertilized Ascaris egg: Elongated, irregular mammillations, disorganized yolk granules.

text: Identify the station and the type of anemia this parasite causes:
options: Anterior end of Strongyloides female - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Anterior end of Enterobius - normocytic normochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - macrocytic megaloblastic anemia
Hookworm copulatory bursa - microcytic hypochromic anemia
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fertilized Ascaris egg that has lost its outer mammillated albuminous coat, leaving a smooth, thick, transparent, colourless chitinous shell.
keyConcept: Decorticated Ascaris egg: Smooth thick shell lacking outer mammillated layer.

text: This parasitic stage is the pathogenic stage of:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Asymmetric, plano-convex (D-shaped) egg with a double-contoured, transparent, smooth shell containing a fully formed, folded, coiled larva.
keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg: D-shaped (plano-convex) with coiled tadpole-like larva.

text: A patient has pallor, puffy eyes and swollen feet. Which figure represents the stage that can be detected in his stool?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma duodenale causes profound microcytic hypochromic iron deficiency anemia (0.2 mL blood loss/worm/day). Diagnostic stage is the thin-shelled 4-8 cell segmented egg.
keyConcept: Hookworm anemia: Blood loss leads to pallor, puffy face, and edema; segmented morula egg.

text: Identify the station and its relevance to man:
options: Cysticercus bovis - it causes human cysticercosis after eating the eggs
Hydatid cyst - man is an accidental intermediate host
Cysticercoid of H. nana - it develops in the human intestinal villi
Cysticercus cellulosae - it can develop in the human brain
Cysticercus bovis - man is infected by eating it in undercooked beef, but it does not develop in man
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Barrel-shaped (lemon-shaped / football-shaped) brown egg with two prominent, transparent, mucoid bipolar plugs, containing an unsegmented ovum.
keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura egg: Barrel-shaped with prominent bipolar albuminous plugs.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Echinococcus granulosus scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia saginata scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia solium scolex - rostellum with hooks
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acid-fast spherical oocysts (4–5 µm) staining brilliant magenta-red on modified Ziehl-Neelsen stain.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum: Acid-fast oocyst.

text: Finding this egg in a stool sample does NOT identify the species of the infecting worm. Interpret.
options: The egg is passed unembryonated, so the hexacanth embryo cannot be examined
The striated shell is dissolved by stool preservatives before examination
Eggs of T. saginata and T. solium are morphologically identical, so the gravid segment or scolex is needed
The egg is identical to the H. nana egg, which is the commonest cause
Eggs of T. solium are passed only in patients with cysticercosis
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical acid-fast oocyst measuring 8–10 µm (twice the size of Cryptosporidium) showing variable acid-fast staining.
keyConcept: Cyclospora oocyst: 8–10 µm spherical, variably acid-fast.

text: This parasitic stage emerges from:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ellipsoidal/spindle-shaped acid-fast oocyst (30 x 12 µm) with tapered ends containing 1 or 2 sporoblasts.
keyConcept: Cystoisospora belli: Large spindle-shaped acid-fast oocyst (30 µm).

text: Fatal hyperinfection with this parasite can occur in patients on corticosteroids. Interpret.
options: Eggs hatch in the stomach and release thousands of larvae
Larvae encyst in muscles and are released by steroids
Rhabditiform larvae turn into filariform larvae inside the gut and re-invade (autoinfection), so the worm load rises sharply when immunity falls
Adult worms multiply asexually in the liver
Steroids stimulate the female to lay unembryonated eggs
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Extremely tiny, oval, refractile microsporidial spores (1–2 µm) with a diagonal horizontal fluorescent/acid-fast polar belt.
keyConcept: Microsporidia: Minute spores (1–2 µm).

text: Structure 1 in this segment is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cephalic cuticular expansion.
keyConcept: Enterobius cephalic alae.

text: Structure 2 in this segment is the:
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Coiled rosette uterus of Diphyllobothrium latum.
keyConcept: Rosette uterus.

text: A carrier of an adult tapeworm developed cysticercosis through autoinfection. Which figure shows the gravid segment of his worm?
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cysticercosis develops exclusively from Taenia solium autoinfection. The gravid segment exhibits 7 to 12 coarse lateral branches.
keyConcept: Taenia solium: 7–12 uterine branches; causes human cysticercosis.

text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Anterior end of Enterobius - cephalic ala
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex of Diphyllobothrium latum is spatulate (almond-shaped) with two longitudinal sucking grooves (bothria), one dorsal and one ventral.
keyConcept: Bothrium: Slit-like sucking groove of Diphyllobothrium latum.

text: This parasite may cause megaloblastic anemia. Interpret.
options: The adult worm sucks blood from the intestinal mucosa
The adult worm in the small intestine takes up large amounts of dietary vitamin B12
The eggs embolize to the bone marrow
Larvae invade the stomach and destroy the parietal cells
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Diphyllobothrium latum absorbs up to 80-100% of host dietary vitamin B12 in the ileum, producing megaloblastic / pernicious-like anemia.
keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum megaloblastic anemia via vitamin B12 competition.

text: Identify the arrowed stage. Why is it infective as soon as it is passed?
options: Giardia lamblia cyst - it already has 4 nuclei
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - it is mature with 4 nuclei
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it sporulates in the colon after 24 hours
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it is passed already sporulated, containing 4 sporozoites
Cryptosporidium parvum oocyst - it contains 8 merozoites
explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum oocysts sporulate inside the host enterocytes and are passed fully mature and immediately infective, containing 4 naked sporozoites.
keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum: Passed fully sporulated with 4 sporozoites (immediate infectivity).
